subject: electrical_engineering

resources.title: Circuits and Electronics
resources.notes: Core EE curriculum covering lumped circuits, MOS devices, amplifiers, energy storage, frequency response, analog/digital circuits, design and laboratory measurement.

resources.title: Signals and Systems
resources.notes: Continuous/discrete-time signals, Fourier/Laplace/Z representations, sampling, LTI systems and applications to feedback, communications and signal processing.

resources.title: Introduction to Electronics, Signals, and Measurement
resources.notes: Practical hands-on electronics, measurement and signals curriculum; explicitly requires no prior electronics experience, supporting a foundation-level entry mapping.

resources.title: NIST Electronics
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology

resources.title: Fundamental Electromagnetic Technologies and Standards
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology

resources.title: Emerging Power Electronic Devices
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology

resources.title: High-Frequency Electronics
resources.provider: National Institute of Standards and Technology

resources.title: Electrical Engineering
resources.notes: Begins with current, voltage, power, units and circuit analysis, then covers amplifiers, semiconductor devices, electrostatics, and signals and systems.

resources.title: University Physics Volume 2: Electricity and Magnetism
resources.notes: Electricity-and-magnetism unit covers fields, potential, current, resistance, DC/AC circuits, magnetic fields, induction, generators, back EMF, inductance and electromagnetic waves. OpenStax currently states that the book may not be ingested into or used to train generative-AI offerings without permission.

resources.title: Electricity and Power-Grid Educational Resources
resources.provider: U.S. Department of Energy Office of Electricity
resources.notes: Electricity 101, grid learning and smart-grid primers explain generation, transmission, distribution, consumption and integration of energy resources.

resources.title: Electric Machines
resources.notes: Graduate course on electromechanical-system principles, machine analysis and design. The provider explicitly notes examples from current research; research mapping denotes exposure to research problems, not independent research competence.

resources.title: Introduction to EECS II: Digital Communication Systems
resources.notes: Introductory undergraduate course covering bits, signals and packets as foundations of digital communication systems; prerequisites remain part of the course context.

resources.title: Introduction to Power Electronics
resources.notes: The first lecture explicitly introduces the history, function, needs and goals of power electronics. Foundation and beginner apply to this introductory lecture only, not to the graduate course as a whole.

resources.title: Digital Circuits Electronics Textbook
resources.notes: Starts with binary numeration and Boolean logic, then covers gates, combinational and sequential circuits, conversion, storage, computing and an introductory digital-communication chapter.

known_gaps: Several foundation cells rely on introductory sections within broader resources and still need redundant hands-on curricula.
Electric machines now has a dedicated graduate curriculum plus introductory physics coverage; a dedicated beginner machine-design course remains desirable.
research portals and metrology programs are evidence/reference layers and do not by themselves establish graduate or research learner readiness
notes: Mappings use the exact electrical_engineering taxonomy keys already present in the manifest.
MIT courses provide assessed curriculum material; NIST/NREL resources remain research, standards, measurement and grid reference infrastructure.
No source is promoted to levels or subsubjects it does not directly support.
Level mappings are resource-specific: an introductory lecture may be foundation-level even when its parent course is graduate-level.
Catalog coverage does not prove ATLAS can ingest, retrieve, cite or apply the material.
